- Can you break out the on-prem/VPC SKU vs. the platform fee (annualized) and the available support tiers?

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the RFI. High level (quick sketch):

1) Licensing model: node-anchored operator licenses + metered inference consumption for hosted components (if used).
2) Platform fee: annual platform fee covers the control plane, observability, and orchestration. Typical amortization options: 12/24/36 months. We can offer a stepped-first-year concession for pilot customers.
3) Support tiers: Standard (business hours, 24/48 response), Premium (24x7 SRE escalation, on-call), Enterprise (designated TAM + quarterly architecture reviews).
4) Migration credit: we can provide a one-time migration credit applied as a percentage of platform fee contingent on commit length; common structure is 30% credit applied against first-year platform fee, amortized if an early exit occurs.

I attached a CSV with a baseline price grid (karthik_vpc_pricing.csv) and our SLA tiers (SLA_tiers.pdf) to give numbers. To make this concrete, can you confirm: target production date, expected average qps per GPU, and whether you need air-gapped / HSM requirements?

I'll loop in Marissa for commercial packaging and Olga for legal/escrow questions once we have your answers.

Cheers,

- Production target: pilot starts mid-August 2026; aim for production ramp Jan 2027.
- QPS: average 1.5k qps across 8 GPUs, but spikes to 6k qps for 30–60s windows.

Would you amortize and clawback, or bill a pro-rata?

Also, are there any limitations on mixing pilot-year reduced platform fee with fixed-node discounts? That is, can we combine a pilot-year platform fee concession with an upfront node discount?

Thanks — if you can send a quick term sketch we can route internally to legal and procurement.

Subject: Nimbus — proposed staged bundle and exit-credit mechanics (internal)

Team — internal note before I propose final sketch to Nimbus: Sarah wants a phased bundle (pilot concession + node discount) and a concrete migration-credit reconciliation example. My suggested approach that balances commercial flexibility and revenue protection:

- Offer: 12-month pilot concession = 40% off platform fee for pilot year (applies only to platform fee, not node licenses).
- Commit: 24-month minimum production commit for full discounts on node SKUs (we can give up to 15% node discount for a 24-month commit).
- Migration credit: provide a 30% credit of the first-year platform fee that is earned on signing, but subject to clawback pro-rata if customer exits before month 24. Practical reconciliation: if they exit at month 15, we compute earned credit = 30% * platform_fee_first_year * (months_active / 24). Un-earned portion is invoiced as a one-time charge. This reduces dispute friction vs. gross clawback.
- Legal: recommend a 90-day notice clause and an escrow for customer data transfer scripts; Olga to advise on specific contract language.

Marissa — can you build a term sheet with these numbers and two variants: (A) pilot concession 40% + 10% node discount, (B) pilot concession 25% + 15% node discount. Include sample P&L for first 24 months.

Karthik

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clarifications. Attaching a clear term sketch and migration-credit example so you can route to procurement/legal: see term_sheet_v1.docx and migration_credit_schedule.xlsx. Summary below: 

Offer summary (two options):

Option A — Pilot-focused (lower upfront burden)
- Pilot year platform fee concession: 40% off platform fee (applies months 0–12)
- Node discount on 24-month commit: 10% off node-anchored licenses
- Migration credit: 30% of first-year platform fee credited at signing and reconciled pro-rata over 24 months; if exit before month 24, un-earned credit is invoiced using the formula in the attached schedule.

Option B — Node-anchored (lower run-rate)
- Pilot concession: 25% off platform fee (months 0–12)
- Node discount on 24-month commit: 15% off node licenses
- Same migration credit mechanics as Option A.

Security & delivery notes:
- We support customer-managed KMS and a VPC-only control plane; escrow for transfer scripts is available (recommended).
- For the brief burst windows you described, we recommend configuring burst nodes or a managed autoscaler; those would be priced separately or treated as a metered add-on.

Next steps:
1) If either option looks aligned, Marissa will produce a redlineable term sheet and a 24-month P&L example (attached).
2) If legal wants clause language, Olga will provide sample exit/migration language.

If this works, happy to hop on a short call with procurement this week to walk through the reconciliation example.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
